paras: The killing of Munroe Bloom was the fatal shooting of a Black man by a Georgia constable at Morrow's Station, on the Central railroad, in mid-March 1882. The constable had warrants charging Bloom and a second Black man with forgery, and Bloom, shot as he resisted arrest, was later found dead in the woods. A coroner's jury ruled the killing justifiable homicide, and the Atlanta dispatch reporting it ran in papers from Richmond and New York to Texas.

According to the Jonesboro News, the constable, identified as Mr. Felix Adamson, L. C., held warrants for the arrest of two Black men "charged with forgery" and found them at Morrows Station. The Marietta Journal gave the officer's name as Constable Felix Anderson.

The only detailed account, printed in the Jonesboro News, follows the officer's version: Adamson told Bloom to consider himself a prisoner, and Bloom refused, drew a pistol, snapped it at the officer and fired once, missing. Adamson returned the fire, "his shot taking effect in the negro's body," and Bloom ran off into the woods. The second man then took Bloom's pistol and fired at Adamson from behind a guano house, fleeing when the constable got a shotgun and opened fire on him.

Adamson went to town for Sheriff Archer, whose hounds followed the second man's trail for several hours before losing it. Adamson did not know he had killed Bloom, the paper said, until someone found the body in the woods.

The coroner's jury returned a verdict of justifiable homicide. The second man had not been captured when the Jonesboro News reported the case, and no later report of his arrest or of charges against the constable appears in the coverage.

The first word came in a brief Atlanta dispatch dated March 16, printed the next day by the New-York Tribune under "Two Negroes Shot by a Constable" and by the Richmond Daily Dispatch under "Shot While Resisting Arrest." Fuller versions of the wire, also carried by the Savannah Morning News and the Dallas Daily Herald, named the dead man only as "Bloom" and added that "the negroes had shot first." The Knoxville Daily Chronicle's version said the men were only "shot at."

Over the following weeks a condensed form of the dispatch, dating the shooting only "a few days ago," circulated in "Southern Gleanings" columns in Tennessee, Alabama, Mississippi and Louisiana weeklies. Georgia papers supplied the names: the Marietta Journal ran a one-sentence item ending "He was resisting arrest," and the Savannah Morning News reprinted the Jonesboro News account, which presented the officer's conduct sympathetically ("Mr. Adamson of course saw his danger") and closed on the coroner's verdict. Every report rested on the officer's account, and none gave a version from Bloom's companion or family.

The papers differ on the officer's surname, Anderson in the Marietta Journal and Adamson, repeated throughout, in the Jonesboro News. The Atlanta dispatch and the Marietta Journal put the shooting on Thursday, March 16, while the Jonesboro News said "Wednesday of last week." The wire also said both men were shot, whereas the local account describes only Bloom as hit.

reader.title: Killing of Munroe Bloom
bases: A constable serving forgery warrants shot and killed Munroe Bloom while trying to arrest him, with no crowd or mob involved (A2, A6, A7).

The Atlanta wire (A1, A2), the Marietta Journal (A6) and the Jonesboro News (A7) independently agree that a constable shot Bloom at Morrow's Station during an attempted arrest and that he was found dead in the woods, though every account of how the shooting began comes from the officer's side.

accounts.label: Atlanta wire report
accounts.gist: Two Black men resisting arrest for forgery were shot by a constable at Morrow's Station; both escaped, but Bloom was later found dead in the woods, and 'the negroes had shot first.'

accounts.label: Marietta Journal
accounts.gist: Munroe Bloom was shot and killed by Constable Felix Anderson on Thursday while resisting arrest.

accounts.label: Jonesboro News (officer's version)
accounts.gist: Adamson told Bloom he was a prisoner; Bloom snapped his pistol and fired once, missing, and Adamson's return shot hit him; the second man then fired at Adamson and fled, and Bloom was later found dead in the woods.

accounts.label: Coroner's jury
accounts.gist: Returned a verdict of justifiable homicide.

framing.detail: Northern and Southern dailies printed the short Atlanta dispatch under headlines such as 'Shot While Resisting Arrest' and 'Two Negroes Shot by a Constable', most adding that the men 'had shot first.'
The Jonesboro News, reprinted in Savannah, told the story from the officer's side ('Mr. Adamson of course saw his danger') and closed on the coroner's justifiable-homicide verdict.
The Marietta Journal gave a one-sentence item naming victim and constable, ending 'He was resisting arrest.'

conflicts.note: The Jonesboro News, a paper from the county where it happened, uses Adamson repeatedly; the Marietta Journal's 'Anderson' is a single mention.
